newsitem.title: FRANCE: French prosecutor to probe Paris region graft.
newsitem.headline: French prosecutor to probe Paris region graft.

text.p: The Paris prosecutor's office on Tuesday opened a probe into suspected large-scale abuses in public works contracts under the Gaullist-led Paris regional council, just two days after the left swept to power in a parliamentary election, judicial sources said.

They said the investigation for "favouritism, fraud, forgery, receiving the proceeds of fraud and anti-competitive practices in public tenders" targeted contracts awarded by the Ile de France regional council, headed by Michel Giraud, a senior member of President Jacques Chirac's Gaullist RPR party.
The investigation targeted "persons unknown", a legal device enabling a magistrate to determine who, if anyone, should be brought to trial for suspected offences.

Sleaze was a major issue in the National Assembly election campaign in the Paris region, with the left accusing Chirac of calling the election almost 10 months early to pre-empt mounting scandals affecting his own party.

The Greens group in the regional council complained last year that Giraud's council had awarded a string of contracts to a single consultancy firm, Patrimoine Ingenierie, from 1989-94. A dissident Gaullist elected official also denounced alleged tender-rigging before being forced to resign last year.
A regional auditor's report sent to Giraud on April 8 condemned "practices aimed at restraining competition", especially in awards of building high schools.
